grandparents_cupboard.reason: Rhubarb, butter, sugar, eggs, almonds and an orange are all plain home-kitchen ingredients.

supermarket.reason: Ground and flaked almonds, forced rhubarb and the other items are everyday stock at Tesco, at ordinary baking prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: Creaming by hand in a bowl and baking in a square tin needs only ordinary kit and beginner technique.

works.reason: The frangipane ratio of 150g butter, 125g sugar, 3 eggs and 200g ground almonds in a 20cm tin, baked at 180°C for 40 to 45 minutes, sets well, and 300g rhubarb on top gives 12 good squares.

honest_times.reason: The cook time is printed as 75 minutes, but the steps give a bake of only 40 to 45 minutes, so the cook time does not match the method.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the ginger appear in the steps, flaked almonds are genuinely almonds, the orange is used for its zest and nothing unlisted is called for.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early April rhubarb is the star topping of a spring afternoon traybake.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is an almond-rich cake with fruit that a family would gladly eat as an afternoon snack, not mostly sugar or refined starch.
